source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 18:1 (what he heard; the pair; the ciphers)
claim_en: va-yishma yitro... et kol-asher ASA ELOHIM le-moshe ('and Jethro heard all that GOD DID for Moses and for Israel'): the did-God pair stands exactly TWICE in the Torah (adjacency checked): MIQETZ's terror ('what is this God has DONE to us,' Gen 42:28 — the brothers at the opened sacks) and Jethro's good news here — the Kitzur: 'in the language in which they grieved, in that language came their relief' (one phrase, the fright and the deliverance); WHAT he heard (the readings named): the sea's split — 'when the sea tore, it roared a great roar until all the kings of east and west heard' — and Amalek's war; and the name's own arithmetic (asserted at the build): YITRO = HA-TORAH (616 = 616) — 'for he came to convert and to receive the Torah'; the Kitzur's further faces named: yeter-plus-vav (six names he bore); the ten utterances plus six-hundred-six commandments atop the sons of Noah's seven (the 613 assembled from his letters).

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 18:8 (the Ramah's three lean rescues)
claim_en: va-YATZILEM YHWH ('and the LORD DELIVERED THEM'): the rescue-verb written LEAN (no yod) — and the Ramah's roster names the Torah's ONLY THREE lean spellings in the whole family ('everywhere else in the Torah, where the yod belongs it is written full'): REUBEN'S rescue of Joseph ('and he delivered him from their hands,' Gen 37:21), the rescue FROM PHARAOH'S SWORD (Eliezer's etymology, 18:4), and the rescue of ISRAEL here (each form census-unique: this one checked, the other two asserted at the build) — TWO of the three lean rescues stand in this one chapter: the corpus notes what the thin trio spans: a brother saving a brother, a God saving a fugitive, a God saving a nation — the deliverance-verb slimmest exactly where deliverance is the story.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 18:5 (the camping pair); Minchat Shai on 18:5
claim_en: el-ha-midbar asher hu CHONE sham ('to the wilderness where he was CAMPING, the mount of God'): the camping-participle stands ONCE in the Torah (checked) — its Scripture-twin the Psalm's angel: 'the angel of the LORD CAMPS around those who fear Him' (Ps 34:8) — the Kitzur: 'Jethro did not need to ask which tent was Moses': he SAW THE CLOUD TIED OVER IT, and by this he recognized it — and that is: the angel of the LORD camps around His fearers' (the address given by the sky over it); MS files the small stroke: the qadma-accent on the guest's own name (va-yavo YITRO); the corpus notes the destination's title: HAR HA-ELOHIM — 3:1's mountain named again, the bush's address now the family's (the readings on the reunion staged at the calling-place, named-only).

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 18:8 (the printed Masorah corrected; the Ramah)
claim_en: al ODOT yisrael ('on account of Israel'): the on-account word with the FIRST vav full and the second lean — and MS convicts the PRINTED MASORAH of corruption: the printed note (which misled even the Menachat Cohen) counts FOUR so written and smuggles in Toledot's well — 'and that is not so: it is the OTHER spelling there in all precise books'; MS's manuscript Masorah and then the Ramah's own register confirm: TWO in the Torah written with the vav after the alef (census exact, checked): Abraham's grief 'on account of HIS SON' (Gen 21:11) and Moses' telling 'on account of ISRAEL' here — the corpus files the pair the true ruling creates: both full-vav on-accounts are on account of A SON (4:22's My-son-My-firstborn: the nation grieved-for and delivered-for under the same spelled word as Ishmael).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 18:9 (the two faces); Minchat Shai on 18:9 (the Mikhlol; the expected-but-not-written)
claim_en: va-YICHAD yitro ('and Jethro REJOICED'): the rejoicing-verb stands ONCE in the Torah (checked) — MS's Masorah: 'none besides' but Job's chilling twin, 'let no JOY enter it' (Job 3:6, the night that wished itself unjoyed — the joy-verb and the joy-ban one skeleton); the Kitzur's two faces: 'he made his heart ONE (echad) to the One God — and became a Jew (yehudi)' / 'his flesh became PRICKLES upon prickles (chidudim) over Egypt's ruin' (the convert rejoicing and shuddering in one verb — the gematria-face named as the tradition's device); MS adds the grammarians' stroke (the dalet dageshed over a silent rest — the Mikhlol's page cited; checked in-token at the build) and the chapter's expected-but-not-written station: asher HITZILO ('that He delivered HIM') — 'one supposes hitzilAM (them), but the reading is hitzilO' (the sevirin class: the grammar bends the nation into a single delivered body).

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 18:10 (the pointing of the blessing)
claim_en: barukh YHWH asher hitzil etkhem ('BLESSED BE THE LORD, who delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh'): MS files the blessing's pointing — the Name under the ZAQEF QATAN (the little-upright pause; mark checked in the SNAPSHOT column): the priest of Midian's doxology filed accent-first by the Masorah; the corpus notes what the machine sees: the first narrated HUMAN blessing of the LORD since Melchizedek's ('blessed be God Most High, who delivered your foes into your hand,' Gen 14:20 — the readings that hang on the parallel, named-only): twice in the canon a foreign priest blesses the Deliverer before Israel's own liturgy exists — and the delivered-verb runs three times in Jethro's mouth and frame (18:9-10) before his creed lands at 18:11.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 18:13 (the court-day letters)
claim_en: va-yaamod ha-am al-moshe min-HA-BOQER ad-HA-AREV ('and the people stood over Moses from THE morning until THE evening'): the narration writes the court-day with BOTH ARTICLES — and when Jethro replays the same span one verse down (18:14) the articles are GONE (min-boqer ad-arev, bare — checked at the build): the Kitzur counts the two extra letters: He and He — 'the judge who judges a true judgment truly is made a PARTNER to the Holy One in the work of creation, WHICH WAS CREATED WITH THE LETTER HE' (the narrator grants the sitting judge the creation-letters; the visitor's complaint strips them); the Kitzur's court-rules beside it (named): ad and not ve-ad — the bench sits until the SIXTH hour; and MI-MACHORAT ('on the morrow') counted to 'the morrow of the Day of Atonement' (the tradition's own with-the-words device, named): the corpus files the checked core — one day, spelled twice, five letters apart, and the difference is the judge's patent of partnership.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 18:15 (the seek-file); 18:16 (the torahs)
claim_en: ki-yavo elai ha-am LI-DEROSH ELOHIM ('for the people come to me TO SEEK GOD'): the phrase's only Torah station (adjacency checked) — the Kitzur's Scripture-four: SAUL seeking over lost donkeys, DAVID over the plague, UZZIAH in war — 'teaching: FOR ALL THEIR NEEDS they came to seek God' (the lost, the sick, the besieged — one verb serves every size of trouble); and the bare seek-verb's Torah-twin is REBEKAH (asserted at the build: 'and she went TO SEEK the LORD,' Gen 25:22 — the corpus's first seeker: a woman with a war in her body; then a nation with a question in its court); ve-hodati et-chuqe ha-Elohim ve-et-TOROTAV — 'and His TORAHS' (plural, BEFORE SINAI): the word Torah-unique in this form (checked at the build) — the Kitzur: its two Scripture-twins stand in EZEKIEL'S TEMPLE-VISION ('a hint to him of the building of the Sanctuary'): the judge's docket already citing the plural law of a house not yet commanded.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 18:18 (the guard-stroke; the printed Masorah corrected)
claim_en: navol tibol... ki-KHAVED mimkha ha-davar ('you will surely WILT... for the thing is TOO HEAVY for you'): MS's letter-file on the diagnosis-verse: the kaf of KI carries the GUARD-STROKE (dagesh after the open vowel; checked in-token) — and ASEHU ('do it') written LEAN: the printed Masorah's note on it ('none like it, and FULL') ruled 'AN ERROR — most Masorah-copies and most precise texts: LEAN, no vav' (the Ramah concurring): the printed-authority file's station lands on the very word Jethro says Moses cannot perform alone — the corpus notes the machine's frame beside it (asserted at the build): KHAVED — the heavy-root's third station in two chapters (Pharaoh's heart, Moses' hands at 17:12, now Moses' CASELOAD): the heaviness that was a verdict, then a wound, is here a workload — and it is the first of the three that DELEGATION can cure.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 18:20 (none like it; Lekach Tov); Kitzur Baal HaTurim on 18:20
claim_en: VE-HIZHARTA ETHEM et-ha-chuqim ve-et-ha-torot ('AND YOU SHALL WARN THEM of the statutes and the torahs'): the warn-word written with a FINAL HE — MS: 'full with He at the end of the word, AND NONE LIKE IT IN THE READING' (census-unique, checked) — and the midrash counts the surplus (Lekach Tov, the Kitzur concurring): the He of ve-hizharta and the He of et-hem — five and five — 'these are the TEN UTTERANCES' (the warning-verb already carrying Sinai's count, two chapters early); MS's file continues down the verse: ha-CHUQIM with the qof dageshed (checked at the build), and the printed-authority station: books that plant ASHER into 'the way they shall walk' — 'they err in it' (the relative-word struck; the way kept bare): the corpus files the crown at its weight: the first TEACHING-command of the judiciary written with one letter no other word in Scripture wears.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 18:19 (the counsel-file); 18:23 (the gate; the place)
claim_en: ata shema be-qoli IATZKHA ('now hear my voice — I WILL COUNSEL YOU'): the counsel-verb stands exactly TWICE in the Torah (census exact, checked): JETHRO here — and BALAAM ('come, I WILL COUNSEL YOU,' Num 24:14): the corpus's two outside counselors under one verb — the builder of Israel's courts and the architect of its snare (the Kitzur's doctrine on the file: Moses HEEDED Jethro's counsel and of him it is said 'he shall come to his place in peace'; ZEDEKIAH refused Jeremiah's counsel — the file's third station, Scripture-side — and was exiled from his place: counsel heard keeps a man his place; counsel refused costs it); and the counsel's own humility named: IM... VE-TZIVKHA ELOHIM — 'if you do this thing AND GOD COMMAND YOU' — the command-word Torah-unique (asserted at the build; its Scripture-twin 'and He command you as RULER,' Samuel): Jethro gates his own advice on the Higher countersignature; AL MEQOMO ('to his place') — the Job-twin named: 'if you judge below, there is peace; if not, judgment is done above — and you shall look on his place, and he is not.'

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 18:21-25 (the roster's letter-file; the Ramah)
claim_en: va-yishma moshe LE-QOL chotno ('and Moses heard THE VOICE of his father-in-law, and did all that he had said'): the voice-word written FULL — the Ramah's rule recited by MS: 'every voice-form in the Torah is written full with vav, except five lean' (the Toledot roster cited; this is not among them — checked at the build against the skeleton): the voice Moses obeys is a full one; the roster's remaining file (all at the build): ASAROT ('of tens') LEAN both times (18:21, 18:25 — the Ramah: 'and all the Torah's likewise lean'); HA-GADOL ('the great [matter]') lean (absent from the Noah-parasha's full-roster); MEOT ('of hundreds') FULL per the precise texts (not among the three lean sealed at Genesis' end); and the one-codex curiosity named: sone-VATZA ('haters of gain') found bound by the binder-stroke in a single manuscript — the corpus files the delegation-chapter's arithmetic in its letters: the tens thinned, the hundreds full, the great matter lean, and the heeded voice alone written whole.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 18:26 (the Mikhlol's stress); Kitzur Baal HaTurim on 18:26
claim_en: ve-et kol-ha-davar ha-qaton YISHPUTU hem ('and every small matter THEY WOULD JUDGE themselves'): the judging-verb in its LONG spelling — Torah-unique (checked) — and the SAME delegation-clause four verses up writes it LEAN (yishptu, 18:22, asserted at the build): the formula repeated with its verb GROWN A LETTER exactly where the judging turns from Jethro's proposal into standing practice (the plan lean, the practice full); MS climbs the grammarians for its stress — 'accented on the final syllable' (the Mikhlol twice, the Shorashim, the Levita's Sefer HaZikkaron named: the long form keeps the long stress); and the Kitzur wires the verse's other end: ha-davar ha-QASHE ('the HARD matter,' brought to Moses) against orpekha ha-QASHE ('your STIFF neck,' Deut 31:27) — 'Moses judged the cases of the STIFF-NECKED' (the hard docket and the hard people one adjective): the corpus files the chapter's closing symmetry: the court stands, the small grows a vav, the hard still climbs to the top.
